passages.heading: Day 1 — The Blank Page
passages.text:
The block in painting is a block on being seen. Welcome to day one of *Daily Painting*. Everything this week is built on a single move — noticing what is already happening inside you before trying to change it.

Every creative freeze is really a fear-of-witness. Naming it dissolves half.

The one-line you'll carry today: **The block in painting is a block on being seen.**

Don't try to make this profound. The whole point of a seven-day arc is that small, honest moves — done in a real body on a real Tuesday — outperform any amount of philosophy. Read the practice once, do it once, and let the rest of the day carry it for you.

passages.heading: Day 2 — Ritual

passages.text:

1. Pick one physical gesture (hand on chest, thumb & finger together, feet firmly planted).
2. Sit calmly and combine it with 3 slow breaths.
3. Repeat 5 times so the pairing sets.
4. Use it once today in real life.

passages.heading: Design Your Minimum
passages.text:
1. Of this week's practices, pick one that took under 3 minutes.
2. Attach it to something you already do daily (morning coffee, closing laptop).
3. Commit to 30 days of that pairing.
4. Write it on paper. Put it where you'll see it.

passages.heading: Day 1 — Notice
passages.text:
police shift lives in your body before it lives in your calendar. Welcome to day one of *Beat Cop Regulation*. Everything this week is built on a single move — noticing what is already happening inside you before trying to change it.

Most people try to solve police shift with better planning. It doesn't work because police shift is a nervous-system state, not a scheduling problem. Today we locate where in the body it actually sits.

The one-line you'll carry today: **police shift lives in your body before it lives in your calendar.**

Don't try to make this profound. The whole point of a seven-day arc is that small, honest moves — done in a real body on a real Tuesday — outperform any amount of philosophy. Read the practice once, do it once, and let the rest of the day carry it for you.

passages.heading: Locate the Charge
passages.text:
1. Sit. Close your eyes.
2. Name the situation of police shift out loud in one sentence.
3. Scan the body top to bottom. Where does the sensation live? Jaw? Chest? Belly?
4. Rest attention there for 60 seconds. Don't fix it. Meet it.

passages.heading: 4-8 Breath
passages.text:
Inhale 4 counts through the nose.
Exhale 8 counts through slightly pursed lips.
Repeat for 10 rounds.
Use this in the first 90 seconds of any police shift spike.

passages.heading: Wide-Angle Attention
passages.text:
1. Close eyes. Hear the furthest sound you can.
2. Feel the weight of your body on the chair.
3. Feel the air on your skin.
4. Now, from this wider place, look at police shift again. It shrinks.

passages.heading: Precise Naming
passages.text:
1. Feel the current wave of police shift.
2. Ask: is it fear, grief, anger, shame, or overwhelm?
3. Get more specific: is it fear of being seen, fear of failing, fear of being alone?
4. Say the precise name out loud. Notice what changes.

passages.heading: Shake It Off
passages.text:
1. Stand up.
2. Shake hands, arms, legs, whole body for 90 seconds. Loose.
3. Then still. Feel the aliveness under the skin.
4. Sit and notice how police shift has changed.
